researcher_notes: Dunkerque LNG (Fluxys) has stated plans to add CO2, ammonia and synthetic-gas import/export business lines (the 'Ammonia Import Terminal' unit), and the Dunkerque l'Energie Creative page confirms the ammonia plan, but it contains no proposal-year tied to that milestone. The likely proposal year is ~2023 (GEM's own value), yet no independent source could be verified that ties the ammonia import terminal to a specific year: the GIIGNL-2024 PDF URL 404s and the Argus capacity article does not contain 'Dunkerque'. Unverifiable to the brief's standard -> UNRESOLVED.

Fos Cavaou's expansion is split into Expansion 1 (technical debottlenecking, capacity raised to ~8 mtpa in May 2023) and Expansion 2 (the larger +2.0 bcm/y step, targeted by 2030, taking the terminal to 11-16.5 bcm/y). Sources (ENTSOG Oct-2022 TYNDP, Argus Dec-2022, GIIGNL) describe Expansion 2 as planned/proposed rather than physically under construction; no independent source confirms a construction-start year for Expansion 2. Cannot verify a year for the construction milestone -> UNRESOLVED (the GEM 'construction/actual' flag here may itself be premature).

The Sinolam LNG terminal was part of the Gas to Power Panama (GTPP) project in Colon. Panama's regulator ASEP revoked Sinolam Smarter Energy's licence in April 2024, halting/shelving the project; this triggered Sinolam's ICSID arbitration ($140M+) and later lawsuits. Three independent Panamanian/Latin-American outlets each report the April 2024 licence cancellation and all contain '2024' + 'Sinolam'. Year = 2024 (shelved when the licence was cancelled).

Telfers FSRU was tied to the Panama NG Power LNG-to-power / Telfers (later Gatun) power-station project (proposed 2013/2014). Multiple search summaries say the 670 MW project lost its licence in December 2017 after failing to reach financial close - the likely cancellation year is 2017 - but no citable URL passed the verifier: the Panama Advisory blog and the Offshore Energy arbitration article both lack the literal '2017' string (the latter is about the 2024 arbitration tribunal) and the chiriqui.life forum returns 403. Year (likely 2017) unverifiable to the brief's standard -> UNRESOLVED.

The Dock Sud LNG terminal (proposed third Argentine import terminal) had its only public activity in October 2016, when YPF/ENARSA began negotiations with Corporacion America. It was never formally cancelled; GEM's 'cancelled (inferred 4 y)' status derives from sustained inactivity (no updates since 2016). No independent source states a cancellation or abandonment year - a 2016 article reports the proposal, not a cancellation, so it cannot be cited as evidence of a cancellation milestone -> UNRESOLVED.

Santos and partners sanctioned the GLNG project via a single final investment decision on 13 January 2011 covering a two-train development; Train 2 (T2) was approved as part of that same FID. The Santos sponsor announcement ('GLNG project sanctioned', primary) and Wikipedia both verify a 2011 FID. Year = 2011.

Fluxys publicly proposed reshaping the Zeebrugge LNG terminal into a multi-molecule hub via its 23 November 2023 call for market interest (open 23 Nov 2023 - 16 Feb 2024) - the project's first public announcement. Fluxys press release (primary) and LNG Prime independent media both verify 2023. Year = 2023.

The Hidrovias do Brasil FSRU (Vila do Conde, Para) was entered in Brazil's October 2019 energy auction but passed over in favour of the Barcarena/New Fortress project; it appeared shelved by November 2021 and is 'cancelled (inferred 4 y)' from sustained inactivity. No independent source states a cancellation year (last substantive coverage is the 2019 auction loss / Feb-2020 planning, none of which asserts a cancellation milestone) -> UNRESOLVED.

Chile's Supreme Court on 12-13 January 2023 rejected the appeals of GNL Talcahuano and the SEA, upholding the annulment of the project's environmental qualification (RCA) and leaving the terminal paralysed/shelved. Two independent Chilean outlets (BioBioChile, El Periodista) verify 2023. Year = 2023 (the court ruling that shelved the project).

The current Puerto Brisa LNG record (Terminal Brisa) documents only the 2021+ revival (TransEnergy 2021 lease; Korean/Energy Developments agreement Nov 2024; status proposed). This 'retired' timeline entry (order 9; pu_id prefix 100001..., an older record lineage than the 100002... peers) appears to mark an earlier Puerto Brisa LNG incarnation/phase being retired before the revival, but I could not locate or verify the year of that retirement from any independent source -> UNRESOLVED.

Genesis Energias signed the Puerto Cortes port/lease contract on 29 January 2024 and began site works in 2024 (first land-preparation works and Chinese-sourced materials observed Dec 2024), constructing an onshore LNG terminal + FSU to supply the Brassavola power plant. Year = 2024 (construction start). Caveat: the two corroborating mastheads, La Prensa and El Heraldo, are both Grupo OPSA titles (common ownership), so not fully independent -> tier medium / independent false, though the 2024 construction-start year is well attested across the coverage.

Snam let its option lapse (July 2023) and Golar's deal to convert the Golar Arctic into an FSRU for the Portovesme (Sardinia) project fell through, announced on Golar's Q2-2023 earnings call (August 2023); the project was effectively shelved in 2023. Three independent outlets (LNG Prime, Splash247, Riviera) verify 2023. Year = 2023.
